text:
lina-support: customer ACME reporting large latency spikes and 500/401 errors since ~2026-03-16 09:12 UTC. They insist they set region=eu-west but traces show routing to us-west. example request id r-0a1b2c3d. Also seeing 401 invalid_token: region_mismatch for some requests. any ideas?

sam-sre: seeing same in router logs — eu-west GPU pool hit 100% queueing at 09:11, router decided to divert a subset of traffic to us-west (spillover policy). that explains the cross-region latency. need auth path confirmed: why are region-scoped tokens rejected when routed to us-west? :eyes:

maya-runtime: auth-service validates token.region_claim if present. by design tokens can be region-scoped for compliance customers. if token.region_claim==eu-west and request lands in us-west we currently reject with 401. we could flip a temporary flag to accept region-mismatch for specific customers, but that's a security/compliance decision. opening a quick mitigation PR to allow fallback for non-enterprise customers.

sam-sre: short-term ops: i can manually scale eu-west pool up 4 nodes to drain queue and revert spillover. can someone confirm the spike source? if it's a short importer job we should prefer queueing until scale completes. autoscaler didn't kick because spike duration < policy.window (5m). we should revisit thresholds.

lina-support: customer reports they also saw 429 queue_full earlier and have unexpected billing for cross-region egress. filed billing ticket. customer wants repro steps and timeline so they can decide whether to rotate tokens or wait.

ben-platform: repro steps (small script):
```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <token-with-region-eu-west>" \
    -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west" \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &\ndone
```
This will create a short, high-concurrency burst that triggers local queueing and can force router spillover if capacity exhausted. check response headers: X-Routed-Region and X-Request-Id.

maya-runtime: mitigation PR opened: feature-flag auth.allow_region_mismatch=true (targeting non-compliant customers). deployed to staging for validation. long-term we should add a router-propagated header (X-Origin-Region) so auth can make informed decisions rather than blind rejects.

alex-eng: long-term fixes: (1) tune autoscaler to react to 1-2m spikes for inference pools that commonly handle bursts; (2) reduce default spillover aggressiveness — prefer short queues over cross-region routing for latency-sensitive traffic; (3) emit routed_due_to_capacity metric and alert when routing > 5% traffic off-region for >3m.

billing-bot: billing ticket BT-882 created for customer ACME — flagged for potential cross-region egress charge.

lina-support: i've informed customer of mitigation steps and asked if they can accept a temporary token acceptance change (non-enterprise only). created internal incident INC-2026-457 and added stakeholders.

sam-sre: manual scale finished, eu-west back to normal at 09:35 UTC, routed-off-region rate dropped to ~0.7%. marking P1 stabilized but requesting postmortem. follow-ups: autoscale tuning, router policy change, auth header change, and billing reconciliation. :white_check_mark:

maria-eng (via thread): please add a note to roadmap for 'region-aware auth fallback' and coordinate with compliance on acceptable scope.

lina-support: will draft postmortem and share before EOD.
